neighbours.label: ' has' (Spanish ' tiene') directly after a fronted 'How many/What N' question phrase and before the subject ('How many goals has Martin scored'); quiet when the subject comes first or the auxiliary is 'have'/'did'
fire: How many patents has the company filed since January?
What steps has the council taken to repair the roads?
How many novels has Margaret written so far?
What explanation has the minister given for the delay?
How many matches has Arsenal lost at home this year?
What evidence has the prosecution presented to the jury?
How many awards has the film received abroad?
quiet: The company has filed many patents since January.
The council has taken steps to repair the roads.
Who has written the most novels so far?
What explanations have the ministers given for the delay?
How many matches did Arsenal lose at home this year?
The prosecution has presented its evidence to the jury.
Tu vecina tiene tres hijos ahora.
Which awards did the film receive abroad?

notes: Probes: 'How many goals has Martin' 1.01, 'What measures has the government' 0.85, 'How many medals has Norway' 0.64, 'Cuántos libros tiene tu hermano' 0.48; subject-first, 'Who has', 'have the students', 'did she' all under 0.05.
